Earlier this year, WhatsApp introduced parent-managed accounts for children under thirteen. Today, WhatsApp is further extending its parental supervision features to teen accounts, adding group activity notifications and additional restrictions on Meta AI. Details below.

WhatsApp 擴大家長監護功能選項

Earlier this year, WhatsApp announced a series of new features aimed at giving parents greater control over accounts belonging to children under thirteen.

These include letting parents decide who can contact the account and which groups it can join, screening message requests from unknown contacts, and managing its privacy settings, with all changes protected by a parent-set PIN code.

Around a few weeks later, WhatsApp further expanded this feature on iOS, adding a dedicated "Parental Supervision" section within the Settings app to make it easier for parents to find and configure managed accounts.

Today, WhatsApp is once again expanding these supervision features—this time extending parental controls from children under thirteen to teens, while giving parents clearer visibility into their children's group activity, more say over how teens interact with Channels and status updates, and the same applies to the use of Meta AI, which may be even more important.

With this update, parents can now receive notifications when a teen joins or leaves a group, as well as when a group they are already in sees a "significant increase" in membership. Parents can also now choose how teens use Channels, whose status updates they can see, and who can see the status updates they post.

As for Meta AI, parents can now choose between the standard experience designed for users thirteen and older, and a more restrictive "Limited Content" option, depending on what they feel is appropriate for their child.

WhatsApp says the "Limited Content" setting will further restrict the topics teens can discuss with Meta AI. Once enabled, Meta AI features that rely on Private Processing will also become unavailable.

WhatsApp also emphasises that these parental supervision features do not allow parents to read teens' actual messages or call content, as those communications remain protected by end-to-end encryption.
